item.title: Chile's Escondida mine gradually resumes operations after fatal accident
item.description: Operations at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile are being resumed progressively as assessments continue, the world's largest copper mine said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Operations at BHP's (BHP.AX) Escondida mine in Chile are being resumed progressively as assessments continue, the world's largest copper mine said on Thursday. Operations at the mine were suspended [USN:S0N44A00V TEXT:"on Wednesday"] after a worker was killed in an accident while carrying out maintenance work. "The Company continues to assess the conditions for a gradual resumption of Mine activities, taking into account workforce wellbeing, operational readiness, risk controls and applicable authority requirements," the company said in a statement. Other operational areas outside Mine Operations were also paused following the incident, with certain activities continuing at reduced rates. In Chile, mines typically can only resume operations following a fatal accident once safety inspectors verify that conditions are safe. Escondida is located in Chile's northern Atacama Desert. BHP operates the mine, while Rio Tinto (RIO.L) holds a 30% stake and Japan-based JECO Corp owns 12.5%.

item.title: Legendary hoops icon Bob Pettit dies at 93
item.description: Basketball legend Bob Pettit, a Hall of Famer and first winner of the NBA's MVP award, has died. He was 93.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Basketball legend Bob Pettit, a Hall of Famer and first winner of the NBA's MVP award, has died. He was 93. The 11-time NBA All-Star and two-time college All-American at LSU died Wednesday in the New Orleans suburb of Metairie. No cause of death was divulged. "Dad passed away very peacefully at his home in Metairie, on Wednesday, September 23," the Pettit family said in a statement. "He was the most amazing father. The most kind, humble and gentle soul. We are so blessed to have him in our lives and we will miss him dearly." Pettit, a member of the NBA's 75th Anniversary Team, was a two-time NBA MVP, a two-time scoring champion and a four-time All-Star MVP during his 11 seasons (1954-65). He also helped revolutionize the then-new power forward position and was elected to the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 1971. He was Rookie of the Year for the Milwaukee Hawks in 1954-55 before the team moved to St. Louis for the final 10 seasons of Pettit's career. He was MVP in the 1955-56 and 1958-59 seasons and averaged 26.4 points, 16.2 rebounds and 3.0 assists in 792 career regular-season games. The Hawks made nine playoff appearances during his career -- reaching the NBA Finals four times -- and won the 1957-58 championship. Pettit was named MVP of the Finals while averaging 29.3 points and 17.0 rebounds. He became the first player to score 50 points in an NBA Finals game when he hit the mark in the clinching Game 6 victory over the Boston Celtics. The 50 points is still tied for sixth most in NBA Finals history. Elgin Baylor holds the mark of 61, set in 1962 for the Los Angeles Lakers. In 88 career playoff games, Pettit averaged 25.5 points and 14.8 rebounds. Pettit averaged a career-best 31.1 points in 1961-62, finishing third behind legendary Wilt Chamberlain (50.4) as well as Walt Bellamy (31.6). He averaged a career best 20.3 rebounds in 1960-61, which was good for just third behind Chamberlain (27.2) and Bill Russell (23.9). Pettit was one of the game's biggest stars in an era before NBA was regularly on television. He retired at age 32, partly because of a balky knee and also due to a banking opportunity. "The Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame mourns the passing of Bob Pettit, a sleek, skilled big man who revolutionized the forward position during his career," the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame said in a statement. "The 11-time NBA All-Star and 2-time MVP retired as the all-time leading scorer in NBA history and left an enduring legacy. He led the St. Louis Hawks to the 1958 NBA championship over the Boston Celtics. The Basketball Hall of Fame salutes this true giant of the game." The Hawks moved to Atlanta ahead of the 1968-69 season and the franchise paid tribute to Pettit on Thursday. "Beyond his accolades -- including 11 All-Star selections and leading the Hawks to the 1958 NBA Championship -- Bob was a true ambassador for the sport and a role model for countless fans," the team said. "We are grateful for his contributions to our franchise and to basketball history. His retired No. 9 jersey continues to hang proudly at State Farm Arena as a lasting reminder of the impact he made on our organization. We extend our deepest condolences to Bob's family, friends and loved ones during this difficult time." A native of Baton Rouge, Pettit stayed home to play college basketball at LSU. He averaged 27.4 points and 14.4 rebounds in 72 games over three seasons. He was a first-team All-American in 1953-54 when he averaged 31.4 points and 17.3 rebounds. Pettit was a second-team All-American the previous season as a junior. Pettit's 31.4 scoring average was a Southeastern Conference record until another LSU legend, Pete Maravich, surpassed it with a 43.8 average in 1967-68. LSU unveiled a statue outside of the Pete Maravich Assembly Center in 2016. A street in Baton Rouge, Bob Pettit Blvd., is also named after him. After being the second overall pick in the 1954 NBA Draft by the Hawks, Pettit received a then-NBA record rookie record contract of $11,000. "I had only $100 in the bank when I graduated from college," Pettit recalled later, according to LSU, "and $11,000 looked like all the money in the world to me." --Field Level Media

item.title: Saudi Grand Mufti tells troops to be ready to sacrifice their lives fighting Houthis
item.description: Saudi Arabia's top religious authority called on soldiers in the kingdom to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Iran-backed Houthis until the group is ousted from power, a statement posted on the Saudi state news agency said.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Hatem Maher
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia's top religious authority called on soldiers in the kingdom to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Iran-backed Houthis until the group is ousted from power, a statement posted on the Saudi state news agency said. The rare and strongly worded message by Saudi Grand Mufti Sheikh Saleh bin Fawzan Al-Fawzan was addressed to soldiers stationed at the country's borders and drew heavily on Quranic verses and recorded sayings of the Prophet Mohammad related to sacrifice and struggle in defence of God. It comes after weeks of escalating violence between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis which has seen the Iran-backed group attack the kingdom with salvos of missiles and drones and Saudi Arabia respond with airstrikes. Observers have been questioning whether Saudi Arabia will launch a broader military operation along with Yemeni government forces it backs. "Protecting this great nation... and punishing anyone who seeks to lay a hand on even an inch of its territory are among the greatest duties and most virtuous acts of devotion, for which lives and souls may be sacrificed in seeking God's pleasure," said the statement, issued late Thursday. Asserting the authority of the Saudi-backed internationally recognized Yemeni government over the entire country was "among the most pressing obligations," it added. Those government forces lost control of the vital Bab el-Mandeb waterway to the Houthis two weeks back, a blow to the kingdom, which has been mired in the conflict since 2015 after it launched an unsuccessful operation to oust the Houthis from the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The recent fighting is the latest episode in 12 years of civil war in Yemen which had largely been frozen since a 2022 but has escalated again and has become linked to the wider Iran war. "We ask God Almighty to grant you all his support, and to protect our countries and beloved Yemen from all harm. We also ask him to bring about the complete defeat of the Houthi group and those who assist and support them," the statement said. The Mufti's letter adds to a growing religiously centered narrative by authorities in the conservative Sunni Muslim kingdom aimed at discrediting the Houthis, who follow a different sect of Islam. State TV has in recent weeks aired footage of an alleged Houthi strike on a mosque in the kingdom's south, and authorities have also accused the Houthis of launching an attack on Mecca, Islam's holiest site. "It is incumbent upon you, brothers serving on the front lines, to remain constantly prepared to perform your duty, to obey the rulers and your field commanders, and to carry out orders with the utmost precision, as God Almighty commanded the companions of his Prophet to do," the statement said. "You are following in the footsteps of the Prophet's companions, defending the sacred sites of Muslims."

item.title: Trump e CEOs do setor de tecnologia discutirão IA na 3ª feira, diz fonte
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, o republicano Mike Johnson, e CEOs do setor de tecnologia realizarão uma reunião sobre inteligência artificial na próxima terça-feira, informou na noite desta quinta-feira uma fonte a par do encontro previsto.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, o republicano Mike Johnson, e CEOs do setor de tecnologia realizarão uma reunião sobre inteligência artificial na próxima terça-feira, informou na noite desta quinta-feira uma fonte a par do encontro previsto. As principais empresas de inteligência artificial do mundo alertaram para os riscos que a IA representa para a humanidade, fazendo um apelo aos governos que trabalhem juntos para gerenciar essa tecnologia cada vez mais poderosa. Governos em todo o mundo têm enfrentado dificuldades para acompanhar os rápidos avanços na IA. A reunião havia sido noticiada anteriormente pela Axios. Não foram divulgados detalhes. Os Estados Unidos e a China, as duas principais potências no desenvolvimento de IA, adotaram abordagens diferentes em relação à regulamentação. Trump argumentou que os EUA não precisam de novas regulamentações específicas para a IA, enquanto a China impôs regras que regem os algoritmos de IA e os dados de treinamento, incluindo a exigência de que o conteúdo gerado por IA seja claramente identificado. Trump disse aos líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU na terça-feira que “rejeita qualquer tentativa de construir um esquema globalista para controlar” a IA, descrevendo a tecnologia como incrível, mas observando que os EUA agirão com cautela.

item.title: BHP dice labores en chilena Escondida se reanudan a medida que avanzan evaluaciones tras accidente
item.description: Las operaciones en la mina Escondida de BHP en Chile se reanudan de forma progresiva mientras prosiguen las evaluaciones tras un accidente fatal, informó el jueves la mayor mina de cobre del mundo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las operaciones en la mina Escondida de BHP en Chile se reanudan de forma progresiva mientras prosiguen las evaluaciones tras un accidente fatal, informó el jueves la mayor mina de cobre del mundo. Las operaciones se suspendieron el miércoles después de que un trabajador falleciera en un accidente mientras realizaba labores de mantenimiento. "La compañía continúa evaluando las condiciones para una reanudación gradual de las actividades mineras, teniendo en cuenta el bienestar de la fuerza laboral, la preparación operativa, los controles de riesgo y los requisitos de las autoridades competentes", dijo en una declaración. Otras áreas operativas ajenas a las operaciones de mina también se paralizaron tras el incidente, aunque ciertas actividades continuaron a un ritmo reducido, agregó. En Chile, usualmente las minas solo reinician faenas tras un accidente fatal una vez que las autoridades verifican que las condiciones son seguras. Escondida está en el norteño desierto de Atacama y asocia a BHP con Rio Tinto (RIO.L) y la japonesa JECO.

item.title: North Korea says South Korea a target if it becomes US collective defence hub
item.description: North Korea said on Friday that South Korea would become a "decisive target" for collective retaliation if it served as a central hub in a US-led collective defence system, state media KCNA reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said on Friday that South Korea would become a "decisive target" for collective retaliation if it served as a central hub in a US-led collective defence system, state media KCNA reported. In a KCNA commentary, Kang Chol Su, described as a department director at the Institute for Enemy State Studies, accused Washington of turning its ally South Korea into a base for pursuing global hegemony and using it as a platform to deploy first in overseas conflicts. Kang cited remarks by the commander of US Forces Korea portraying South Korea as a key centre of collective defence and criticised joint drills and US deployments. The commentary said Pyongyang had prepared countermeasures and would ruthlessly crush challenges to its security. US Forces Korea did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The United States stations about 28,500 military personnel in South Korea to help deter aggression from North Korea.

item.title: Iran's president says it is up to US to choose if it wants to end Iran war
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said it was up to the United States to choose when the Iran war will end, when asked if the conflict could end by the end of the year.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said it was up to the United States to choose when the Iran war will end, when asked if the conflict could end by the end of the year. "But we do not wish to continue. It's America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not," Pezeshkian said, responding to the question in an interview aired on Thursday on Fox News' "Special Report with Bret Baier" show. Iran's president told the UN General Assembly on Wednesday Tehran would never surrender to US pressure as the two sides have remained far apart on how to end the war. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he could "[USN:L8N45E0CI TEXT:"annihilate"]" Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon. Trump has [USN:L4N4061X8 TEXT:"offered shifting goals"] and timelines for the war that began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have [USN:L1N3ZR14Q TEXT:"killed thousands"] and [USN:L6N3ZY0Q0 TEXT:"displaced millions"]. Trump has cited weakening Iran's nuclear capabilities as one of his war objectives. Iran, which does not have nuclear weapons, denies seeking them. The US is nuclear-armed. Tehran says it has the right to develop nuclear technology for peaceful purposes as a party to the nuclear [USN:L1N42N0IE TEXT:"Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)"].

item.title: Insurance Australia Group settles $2 billion Credit Suisse lawsuit over Greensill collapse
item.description: Insurance Australia Group said on Friday its unit had agreed to settle a A$2.8 billion ($1.96 billion) Credit Suisse lawsuit over losses linked to finance firm Greensill Capital.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Insurance Australia Group (IAG.AX) said on Friday its unit had agreed to settle a A$2.8 billion ($1.96 billion) Credit Suisse lawsuit over losses linked to finance firm Greensill Capital. Here are some key details: The insurer did not disclose the terms of the settlement citing confidentiality. The aggregate face value of the claimed amounts in the Credit Suisse Proceedings was about A$2.8 billion plus interest, Insurance Australia said. The proceedings relate to policies issued by Insurance Australia's unit BCC Trade Credit to Greensill entities. The settlement comes just months after Insurance Australia agreed to settle a A$4 billion lawsuit by the administrators of Greensill Bank. The 2021 collapse of Greensill Capital led Credit Suisse to wind down $10 billion in funds linked to the firm. Last year, Credit Suisse had [USN:L5N3VW0J0 TEXT:"lost"] a $440 million lawsuit against SoftBank Group Corp (9984.T) over funds Greensill had lent to Katerra, a construction company backed by the Japanese group. UBS Group, which took over Credit Suisse after its 2023 collapse, did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Insurance Australia said the remaining proceedings brought by White Oak against its unit Insurance Australia Limited remain ongoing, with the aggregate face value of claim amounts at nearly A$170 million. The insurer said the Credit Suisse settlement would not have a material impact on its 2027 financial results. ($1 = 1.4261 Australian dollars)

item.title: Reino Unido adverte Irã de que não tolerará atividades hostis em solo britânico, segundo reportagem da Sky News
item.description: O ministro das Relações Exteriores britânico, Ed Miliband, disse ao ministro das Relações Exteriores iraniano, Abbas Araqchi, durante uma reunião, que o Reino Unido “não tolerará intimidações, ameaças ou atividades hostis em solo britânico” por parte de grupos ligados ao país dele, informou a Sky News nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro das Relações Exteriores britânico, Ed Miliband, disse ao ministro das Relações Exteriores iraniano, Abbas Araqchi, durante uma reunião, que o Reino Unido “não tolerará intimidações, ameaças ou atividades hostis em solo britânico” por parte de grupos ligados ao país dele, informou a Sky News nesta quinta-feira. Miliband e Araqchi se encontraram à margem da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova York, segundo a reportagem, citando o Ministério das Relações Exteriores britânico. Os dois discutiram a guerra no Oriente Médio, a importância da reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz e a “determinação inabalável do Reino Unido de combater ameaças de grupos ligados ao Irã em solo britânico”, acrescentou a reportagem. O Centro Nacional de Segurança Cibernética do Reino Unido informou na semana passada que agentes cibernéticos ligados ao Estado iraniano haviam usado uma família de spywares conhecida como “CHOSEN BRICK” para roubar emails, mensagens e outras informações confidenciais por meio de campanhas de “spear-phishing” em plataformas de mensagens, incluindo WhatsApp e Telegram. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores, da Comunidade Britânica e do Desenvolvimento do Reino Unido não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

item.title: US edge International team in tight Presidents Cup opener
item.description: The United States began their bid for an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title with a 3-2 lead over the International Team after Thursday's opening fourball session at Medinah Country Club outside Chicago.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States began their bid for an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title with a 3-2 lead over the International Team after Thursday's opening fourball session at Medinah Country Club outside Chicago. Justin Thomas and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun put the first point on the board for the Americans with a 4&3 victory over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria. Koivun made two early birdies as the Americans took control, and they never trailed before the Internationals conceded the 15th. The victory extended Thomas' unbeaten record in Presidents Cup fourballs to 7-0-0. "It was fun to be out there with Jackson and watch him do his thing. He's really impressive to watch, and I'm really happy he's on my team," Thomas said. The Internationals quickly answered through Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune, who beat Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele 3&1 to level the session at 1-1. The Japanese pair moved two up after nine holes and held off a late challenge from the Americans, with Hisatsune answering Young's birdie at the 15th before the Internationals closed out the match. "I'm just lucky," Hisatsune said. "Playing with Hideki, he's also a friend, so (he) gives me more trust every single time." SCHEFFLER, BURNS HOLD ON Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns restored the US lead with a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, finally earning a Presidents Cup win together after struggling to convert previous opportunities. The Americans raced into an early four-hole lead but saw it disappear, and Im moved the Internationals ahead at the 13th. Burns immediately responded with a birdie at the next hole, hitting an eight-iron to a couple of feet. "It was kind of a key moment in our match just to kind of snatch back some of that momentum," Burns said. Scheffler then produced the shot of the match at the last, recovering from a bunker to within tap-in range and leaving Im needing a long birdie putt to keep the match alive. Im missed, allowing the world number one and Burns to close out the win. "I felt like, if I could make a nice bunker shot in there, it would really put a lot of pressure on him in order to have to make his putt in order to tie the match," world number one Scheffler said. "It was probably just a little bit of a sigh of relief to finally get a point and just kind of let that out," Burns said. Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa then extended the US advantage with a dominant 3&2 victory over Adam Scott and Ryan Fox, giving the Americans a two-point cushion heading into the final match. The US pair led from the opening hole and maintained their advantage despite failing to capitalize on several chances in the middle of the round. Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim cut the deficit to 3-2 with a 3&2 win over Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay in the final match. The South Koreans moved two up early, were pegged back to all square and then regained control before closing out the match at the 16th. "We did a really good job of just managing momentum and really choosing the holes to attack," Tom Kim said. "It helps when your partner makes a lot of birdies." Tom Kim's tee shot on the 16th nearly produced an ace, hitting the flagstick before spinning away, but the Internationals had already secured the match. The biennial team event features 30 matches over four days, with the first team to reach 15.5 points winning the Presidents Cup. Friday's schedule features five foursomes matches, with fourballs and foursomes sessions to follow on Saturday before Sunday's 12 singles. The US have won the Presidents Cup 13 times, lost once and tied once, with their only defeat coming in 1998 and the lone tie in 2003.

item.title: Trump, US House speaker and tech CEOs to meet on AI on September 29, source says
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Republican House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson and tech CEOs will hold a meeting on artificial intelligence on September 29, a source familiar with the planned meeting said late on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump , Republican House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson and tech CEOs will hold a meeting on artificial intelligence on September 29, a source familiar with the planned meeting said late on Thursday. The world's leading artificial intelligence companies have warned of the risks posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology. Governments around the world have struggled to keep pace with rapid advances in AI. The planned meeting was reported earlier by Axios. Further details were not immediately available. The United States and China, the two leading powers in AI development, have taken different approaches to oversight. Trump has argued the US does not need new AI-specific regulations, while China has imposed rules governing AI algorithms and training data, including requirements that AI-generated content be clearly labeled. Trump told world leaders at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday he "rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control" AI, describing the technology as amazing but noting the US would be careful.

item.title: Polymarket sues New York attorney general to block regulation of its prediction market
item.description: Polymarket sued New York Attorney General Letitia James and other state officials on Thursday evening, to block them from regulating its prediction market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Presidente iraniano diz que cabe aos EUA decidir se querem pôr fim à guerra com o Irã
item.description: O presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, afirmou que cabe aos Estados Unidos decidir quando a guerra com o Irã chegará ao fim, ao ser questionado se o conflito poderia terminar até o final do ano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, afirmou que cabe aos Estados Unidos decidir quando a guerra com o Irã chegará ao fim, ao ser questionado se o conflito poderia terminar até o final do ano. “Mas não queremos continuar. São os Estados Unidos que precisam decidir se querem encerrar isso ou não”, disse Pezeshkian, respondendo à pergunta em uma entrevista exibida nesta quinta-feira no programa “Special Report with Bret Baier”, da Fox News. O presidente do Irã disse à Assembleia Geral da ONU na quarta-feira que Teerã nunca se renderia à pressão dos EUA, já que os dois lados continuam com posições muito distantes sobre como encerrar a guerra. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, disse na terça-feira que poderia “aniquilar” o Irã caso não haja um acordo para encerrar a guerra, mas também sugeriu que um acordo poderia ser alcançado em breve. Trump tem apresentado metas e prazos variáveis para a guerra que começou em 28 de fevereiro, quando os EUA e Israel atacaram o Irã e Teerã respondeu com seus próprios ataques contra Israel e países do Golfo que abrigam bases norte-americanas. Os ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã e os ataques israelenses ao Líbano mataram milhares de pessoas e deslocaram milhões. Trump citou o enfraquecimento das capacidades nucleares do Irã como um de seus objetivos de guerra. O Irã, que não possui armas nucleares, nega estar buscando obtê-las. Teerã afirma ter o direito de desenvolver tecnologia nuclear para fins pacíficos, como signatário do Tratado de Não Proliferação Nuclear (TNP).

item.title: US Democrats criticize lavish Trump-Xi summit as lacking substance
item.description: US Senate Democrats criticized President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, saying it prioritized pageantry over substance on issues such as artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and weapons for Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: US Senate Democrats criticized President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, saying it prioritized pageantry over substance on issues such as artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and weapons for Taiwan. Trump welcomed Xi to the White House for a [USN:L1N45F0US TEXT:"state summit"] heavy on diplomatic honors, but with no sign that closed-door talks yielded breakthroughs on the issues dividing them. In a statement signed by at least 19 of the 47 members of the Democratic caucus and seen by Reuters, the Democrats called on Trump to immediately deliver more than $15 billion in security assistance — $1.3 billion in funds and a $14 billion arms sale package — that Congress has approved for Taiwan and to push for human rights and the release of wrongfully detained Americans. Some of Trump's fellow Republicans also marked the summit by [USN:L1N45F0LQ TEXT:"calling on Trump"] to release the funds for Taiwan. The Democrats also criticized Trump's loosening of restrictions on high-end chip sales to China, and said that the extension of the US-China tariff truce does not sufficiently address supply chain issues such as China's hold on global rare earth refining. "We will compete successfully with China only through sustained investment in our own strengths, close coordination with allies, and an unwavering defense of our democratic values," the statement said. Democrats are typically critical of Trump's policies, but their response to the summit gave an indication of how party members might address Beijing if they take control of one or both houses of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections. Polls show that Trump's Republicans will struggle to keep their slim majorities in Congress in the upcoming contest, as the president's approval rating drops.

item.title: Tesla set to formally roll out Semi electric trucks at Nevada event
item.description: Tesla is set to roll out its Semi trucks late on Thursday at an inauguration of its plant in Sparks, Nevada, the EV maker said on its website and social media, almost nine years after CEO Elon Musk unveiled the electric big rigs.
item.dc:creator: Abhirup Roy
item.content:encoded: Tesla (TSLA.O) is set to roll out its Semi trucks late on Thursday at an inauguration of its plant in Sparks, Nevada, the EV maker said on its website and social media, almost nine years after CEO Elon Musk unveiled the electric big rigs. The Semi, designed for long-haul freight with a range of up to 500 miles, was first unveiled in 2017 and production was expected to start in 2019. The first truck eventually rolled off the high-volume production line in April and volume production was set to start this year. However, Tesla's July shareholder letter said that production of Semi would begin in 2026, removing an earlier forecast for volume production this year. The Semi expands the market for Tesla, known for its electric sedans and SUVs, into commercial freight haulers at a time when diesel prices in the United States have soared to record highs. Tesla began limited deliveries to customers including PepsiCo in the US in late 2022. Delays, rising competition and reversal in EV policies in the United States have since raised concerns about demand. Still, Tesla this week received an order for 2,500 Semis from a coalition of the world's largest cargo-owning shippers, including Microsoft and PepsiCo, according to clean transportation nonprofit Catalyst Mobility. That is nearly double the existing US fleet of electric Class 8 trucks, the nonprofit said. Last month, Swedish freight technology company Einride AB announced a deal to add 500 Semi trucks to its fleet. Tesla had said the Nevada factory was being set up to run at an annual capacity of up to 50,000 units. Tesla investors and fans online have said they expect details on how Tesla plans to ramp up production of Semis, prices, and names of major customers.

item.title: Beyond high-profile wars, a worldwide battle for resources
item.description: According to Pakistani media, the militants who stormed a lithium mining site in Balochistan last month had a simple message as they destroyed equipment and briefly detained employees: they were no longer prepared to tolerate mining operations in the region, and foreign and local mining firms should stay away.
item.dc:creator: Peter Apps
item.content:encoded: According to Pakistani media, the militants who stormed a lithium mining site in Balochistan last month had a simple message as they destroyed equipment and briefly detained employees: they were no longer prepared to tolerate mining operations in the region, and foreign and local mining firms should stay away. As wars in the Middle East and Ukraine grabbed headlines and the United States and China navigated their still largely bloodless face-off, culminating in the meeting of President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping this week, a host of other overlapping confrontations over resources have ranged elsewhere in the world throughout 2026. Behind the scenes, the US, European Union and Pacific governments, particularly Japan, South Korea, Australia and Taiwan, are already locked in a still-escalating high-stakes race to uncouple themselves from China when it comes to the key resources driving modern tech. Rare earths and minerals continue to fuel conflict in central Africa, while Sudan’s ongoing civil war is now largely fuelled by gold smuggling that fills the coffers of groups intent on ethnic violence. Some of that will have been discussed in New York this week at the annual United Nations General Assembly bringing world leaders together – but much of this global confrontation now takes place behind the scenes, albeit with starkly rising stakes. In the Gulf, the US-Iran conflict sparked by the launch of the US-Israeli "Operation Epic Fury" – now widened to include a worsening face-off between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi rebels – now threatens an energy supply shock that might significantly derail global growth. In the short term, significant amounts of the energy of the UN gathering were consumed by discussions over the safety of fast-evolving artificial intelligence models, with OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman and others briefing the Security Council. Discussions over Ukraine have also included a potential suspension by both sides of attacks on energy infrastructure. In the background, however, the at least equally high-stakes confrontation taking place is over the raw materials necessary for that ongoing computing and wider technological revolution – including copper for almost every form of circuitry, lithium batteries and a host of other rarer earths and other minerals. In June, the European Commission joined the US State Department-coordinated “Pax Silica”, a Washington-led collective of more than two dozen nations that commenced with an agreement between the US and Japan in September and has expanded since to include much of Europe, as well as key Pacific allies. Still, according to consultancy AlixPartners, Beijing still accounts for up to 70% of rare earth mining, 85% of refining capability and 90% of rare earth metal alloy and magnet production. According to industry experts, the latter remains a pinch point for both aerospace and cutting-edge chip manufacturers – and so far, foreign diplomats in Washington say the US continues to struggle to regain that initiative. That makes the battle for resources in places like Pakistan and central Asia particularly important – even while the limits of reporting and established fact can make that hard to track. What is clear, however, is that they are already very much part of that wider confrontation. BALOCHISTAN MINING TARGETED According to global monitoring NGO ACLED – which stands for Armed Conflict Location and Event Data – mining interests in Balochistan have been targeted on at least 40 separate occasions so far in 2026. Local media now detail a wider range of incidents taking place almost every day, including an ambush and firefight of almost three dozen mining vehicles at the end of August that left at least 13 militants dead. Other stories tell of suspected militants detained and then found dead, victims of suspected extrajudicial killings by government personnel or private security. Who is behind the several overlapping groups of ethnic Baloch militants remains hotly disputed. Pakistan routinely blames India’s Research and Analysis Wing intelligence agency, known as RAW, for coordinating and arming the attacks, something India denies. The region is the poorest in Pakistan, with guerrilla fighters reportedly crossing the border from Iran and Afghanistan. What is not in doubt is their mounting opposition to Chinese mining interests, which has intensified sharply in recent years. The US has condemned the attacks as terrorism, but not commented in more detail – although the government in Islamabad has increasingly presented itself to the Trump administration as an appealing partner, including as a source of resources. Visiting Trump in the Oval Office in October 2025, Pakistan's military chief and de facto ruler Asim Munir brought with him a wooden display case of minerals before signing a $500 million memorandum of understanding. While mining currently makes up less than 1% of Pakistani GDP, the government claims it has as much as $6 trillion in undeveloped reserves. Amongst the largest projects is the Reko Dik gold and copper mine, unusually for Pakistan one by Canadian firm Barrick rather than a China-based conglomerate. The multi-vehicle convoy ambushed at the end of August was returning from the mine, due to enter production in 2029. OTHER RESOURCE FLASHPOINTS Other nations increasingly in the crosshairs of global resource competition include those in Central Asia. In June, Kazakhstan became the first nation in that region to sign up to the US-run “Pax Silica” – but it appeared to alienate Washington by also joining the China-run World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO) barely three weeks later. That prompted an immediate warning from the US State Department that membership of the “Pax Silica” collective was irreconcilable with joining rival Chinese entities. But in reality, Washington will always seek to continue to build new resource deals with the Kazakhstan government, which oversees some of the world’s largest stockpiles of uranium as well as chromite, copper, beryllium, tantalum, lead and zinc. The US hosted all five major Central Asian powers at a critical mineral summit last November, striking further deals with Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. South Korea hosted its own critical mineral summit this month with several Central Asian governments, while Japanese media reported this week that Tokyo would launch its own strategy next year with a similar goal. Japan is also now at the forefront of what is now often described as “urban mining”. In April, a quartet of Japanese companies announced they would use robots to recover neodymium magnets critical to computer hard drives from old air-conditioners. Other firms are pushing ahead with undersea remote mining projects to tap resources previously unreachable. The Trump administration also has a range of commercial and diplomatic outreach underway in Latin America, keen to push back against the previous dominance of Chinese extractive firms in the “Lithium Triangle” of Chile, Argentina and Bolivia – although despite that, Chinese trade with South American nations has continued to rise sharply in the current year. In the Oval Office this week, Trump and Xi might have tried to look like two geopolitical titans dividing the world between them. But the reality on the ground is already considerably messier, and the scramble for resources in the new industrial age is only just beginning.

item.title: KKR-backed e-bus maker PMI Electro confidentially files for India IPO
item.description: KKR-backed electric bus maker PMI Electro Mobility Solutions has confidentially filed draft papers for an initial public offering in Mumbai, a newspaper advertisement showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: KKR-backed (KKR.N) electric bus maker PMI Electro Mobility Solutions has confidentially filed draft papers for an initial public offering in Mumbai, a newspaper advertisement showed on Friday. Founded in 2017, PMI Electro Mobility is an electric commercial vehicle manufacturer with a fleet of 3,300 e-buses across 34 cities in India. US private equity firm KKR had earlier this year [USN:L4N4060KQ TEXT:"invested"] around $310 million in PMI Electro Mobility Solutions and its e-bus platform Allfleet India. PMI Electro competes with listed rivals Olectra Greentech (OLEC.NS) JBM Auto (JBMA.NS) and Tata Motors (TATM.NS) in India. Under India's confidential filing process, companies can submit draft IPO documents to the market regulator without making them public, allowing them to shield sensitive financial and business information while seeking regulatory feedback. (This story has been refiled to correct the dateline to Sept 25.)

item.title: UK consumer confidence hits more than two-year high in September, GfK says
item.description: British consumer confidence unexpectedly struck a more than two-year high this month as households grew more optimistic about their personal finances, according to a survey on Friday that added to recent signs of resilience in the economy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British consumer confidence unexpectedly struck a more than two-year high this month as households grew more optimistic about their personal finances, according to a survey on Friday that added to recent signs of resilience in the economy. Market research firm GfK's Consumer Confidence Barometer rose to -13 in September, up one point from last month and marking its highest level since August 2024, shortly after the governing Labour Party came to power. A Reuters poll of economists had pointed to a fall to -16. • GfK said consumers' confidence in the economic outlook also rose to its highest level since August 2024, while the mood around personal finances hit an eight-month high • Neil Bellamy, consumer insights director at GfK, said the deteriorating inflation outlook could start to weigh on households • "While the headline score continues to improve, confidence is still firmly in negative territory. With inflation, energy and fuel prices rising, could we soon see consumer sentiment falter?" he said • Separate consumer confidence readings from YouGov/Cebr and LSEG/Ipsos published this month hit their highest readings since February • Surveys from BRC/Opinium and S&P Global have shown a fall in consumer confidence

item.title: UK regulatory crackdown closes CFD firms with overseas links
item.description: Britain's Financial Conduct Authority said on Friday that 21 firms offering CFDs had closed since 2025, three others were cancelling their regulatory permissions to trade and two face investigation after a crackdown on misleading customers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Financial Conduct Authority said on Friday that 21 firms offering CFDs had closed since 2025, three others were cancelling their regulatory permissions to trade and two face investigation after a crackdown on misleading customers. The regulator did not name the firms offering contracts-for-differences, which are complex financial products used to bet on the price of a wide range of assets without owning them. The FCA has been [USN:L6N3WP0MG TEXT:"cracking down"] on CFD providers since it restricted their sale to retail customers in 2019. It said CFD firms that do little business in Britain, but use their authorisation to lend credibility to linked overseas businesses, led people to think they were dealing directly with a UK-regulated firm and would benefit from UK protections. "Consumers need to know exactly who they're dealing with and what protections they have," Dominic Holland, the FCA's director of sell-side supervision, said in a statement. "When firms blur the lines between their UK-regulated activities and overseas businesses, we will step in," he added. Retail customers who trade CFDs through FCA-authorised firms can access the Financial Ombudsman Service to raise complaints, receive potential compensation in the event of firm failures, have limits placed on leverage and a range of other protections.

item.title: Yankees, Orioles move up Saturday game into Friday twin bill
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles and host New York Yankees won't play Saturday due to inclement weather anticipated to hit the Northeast.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Orioles and host New York Yankees won't play Saturday due to inclement weather anticipated to hit the Northeast. Instead, the American League East rivals will play a single-admission doubleheader on Friday, with Game 1 slated for 4:05 p.m., three hours ahead of the original game time. If Game 1 ends later than 6:35 p.m., then Game 2 will begin about 30 minutes later, not before 7:05. The Yankees said tickets for Saturday's game will not be honored for the Friday doubleheader. The Yankees (91-67) are locked into the first wild-card spot in the American League since the Tampa Bay Rays (96-62) clinched the East title with a win at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday. The Orioles (78-81) will miss the playoffs. The Boston Red Sox have made similar arrangements for their regular-season-ending series against the visiting Chicago Cubs. Boston and Chicago will play a split doubleheader Friday and the third game of their series is slated for Saturday night; they will conclude the regular season one day before the rest of baseball, with the effects of a nor'easter expected to affect Boston on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain warns Iran it will not tolerate hostile activity on UK soil, Sky News reports
item.description: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in a meeting that Britain will "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil" from groups linked to his country, Sky News reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in a meeting that Britain will "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil" from groups linked to his country, Sky News reported on Thursday. Miliband and Araqchi met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, the report said, citing Britain's foreign office. Miliband and Araqchi discussed the war in the Middle East , the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Britain's "unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups in UK soil", the report added. Britain's National Cyber Security Centre said last week Iranian state-linked [USN:S8N41P0E1 TEXT:"cyber"] actors had used a spyware family known as "CHOSEN BRICK" to steal emails, messages and other sensitive information through "spear-phishing" campaigns on messaging platforms including WhatsApp and Telegram. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

item.title: OpenAI to preview GPT-6 Cyber within days, Fortune reports
item.description: OpenAI is set to preview a cybersecurity-focused AI model, GPT-6 Cyber, within days and launch a new product designed to help customers deploy it more securely and automatically, Fortune reported on Thursday, citing multiple sources familiar with the plans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI is set to preview a cybersecurity-focused AI model, GPT-6 Cyber, within days and launch a new product designed to help customers deploy it more securely and automatically, Fortune reported on Thursday, citing multiple sources familiar with the plans. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman and rival Anthropic's CEO earlier this month joined [USN:L4N456128 TEXT:"industry leaders"] in calling for a slower pace of AI development and stronger safety measures. Cybersecurity is emerging as one of AI's fastest-growing markets, as tech firms develop tools to combat threats and contain rogue AI agents. OpenAI has warned its flagship [USN:L4N45E133 TEXT:"Astra model"] from the GPT-6 lineup can at times try to evade human oversight, while [USN:L4N45F1EW TEXT:"Australia"] said on Thursday an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June. Fortune said GPT-6 Cyber, OpenAI's fourth cybersecurity-focused model released this year, could be unveiled at the company's DevDay event in San Francisco on Tuesday, along with plans to ship a dozen or more other products. A limited group of customers in OpenAI's application-only Daybreak Red cybersecurity program already has access to GPT-6 Cyber for alpha testing, the report said.

item.title: Oracle, Blue Owl project delay sends ripples through AI financing, sources say
item.description: Oracle's move to protect itself against potential delays at a massive data center project developed by Blue Owl in New Mexico sent a chill through the trillion-dollar market for AI infrastructure financing, according to interviews with bankers and investors.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wang, Isla Binnie, Sabrina Valle
item.content:encoded: Oracle's (ORCL.N) move to protect itself against potential delays at a massive data center project developed by Blue Owl (OWL.N) in New Mexico sent a chill through the trillion-dollar market for AI infrastructure financing, according to interviews with bankers and investors. Oracle [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"issued a force majeure notice"] in connection with Jupiter, a data center campus Blue Owl unit STACK Infrastructure is building to support OpenAI, the latest setback for a sector where lenders and investors are growing more cautious about financing the industry's breakneck expansion. Blue Owl said the notice did not alter the parties' commitment to the project. Even so, the event is reverberating through discussions around other proposed data center financings, including SB Energy, which is developing a campus to serve OpenAI in Ohio, a person close to its financing said. SB Energy decided this week to delay its IPO. Companies can use force majeure provisions when events beyond their control make it difficult to meet their contractual obligations. Lawyers say such provisions are becoming more common in data center development agreements, raising concerns among lenders and investors. "The financing side of the AI buildout is starting to ask much harder questions than the demand side," said Sean McDevitt, a partner at management consulting firm Arthur D. Little. "The underlying demand still appears very strong, but investors and lenders are increasingly focused on how risk is allocated." With interest rates in the US rising to levels last seen two decades ago, Wall Street is intensifying its scrutiny of the economics and the politics of deals that just months ago appeared settled — meaning that the participation in a deal of highly rated firms such as Oracle isn't necessarily enough to soothe anxious investors. The pullback comes as AI-related capital spending by the six biggest US technology companies is projected to reach around $1 trillion in 2027, according to Moody's — raising concerns among lenders about whether markets can absorb the volume of issuance without wider pricing pressure or tighter terms. CASE STUDY Investors and lenders are studying the [USN:L4N43T1OG TEXT:"Oracle situation"] as a real-world example of how contractual protections may be tested and who pays the bill when projects run into delays outside the parties' control, they said. The program is being delayed by a year, said the person familiar with Oracle's notice and the deal. Blue Owl has about $3 billion of equity invested in the project and earns a lower return during construction, with returns increasing once the data center is completed, the person familiar with the terms said. Oracle invoked force majeure due to delays securing power to the site, the person familiar with the matter said. Delaying completion pushes back the start of those higher returns for Blue Owl. As developers race to build AI infrastructure at unprecedented scale, the contracts underpinning those projects are changing quickly, said Rajat Rana, a New York-based partner at law firm Quinn Emanuel. “These contracts are so rapidly evolving. If you look at a data center contract from January this year and a contract today, it's massively different,” he said. At least 45 projects worth $68 billion faced opposition from community groups in the second quarter of 2026, according to research firm Data Center Watch, after 75 projects worth about $130 billion were disrupted in the first quarter. Banks are involved in several projects that face community action. Earlier this year, Blue Owl struggled to syndicate financing for a $4 billion data center project in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, anchored by CoreWeave (CRWV.O) . "Blue Owl, STACK Infrastructure and Oracle remain fully aligned on Project Jupiter. This notice does not change the financial commitments to this multiyear project," the company said. Oracle stock fell 3.5% on Thursday, after media reports of the notice. Blue Owl closed 3.6% lower. Data center developments including Meta's project in El Paso, Texas, and Related Digital's planned $16 billion Oracle-focused campus in Saline Township, Michigan, have faced opposition from residents of those areas. Blackstone's QTS in July said it had terminated its planned Digital Gateway data center project in Virginia and withdrawn the associated filings after years of planning and regulatory review.

item.title: Diamondbacks outslug Rockies for 5th straight win
item.description: Gabriel Moreno and Nolan Arenado homered in a six-run first inning and the surging Arizona Diamondbacks beat the Colorado Rockies 12-8 on Thursday in Denver to continue their drive for a National League wild-card berth.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Gabriel Moreno and Nolan Arenado homered in a six-run first inning and the surging Arizona Diamondbacks beat the Colorado Rockies 12-8 on Thursday in Denver to continue their drive for a National League wild-card berth. James McCann also went deep for Arizona (85-74), which had a season-high 18 hits in its fifth straight win. The Diamondbacks moved within 2 1/2 games of Philadelphia for the third and final NL playoff berth. The Phillies hosted Milwaukee on Thursday night. Arizona, which holds the tiebreaker over Philadelphia, is assured that at least the first game of its three-game series at San Diego beginning on Friday night will have postseason implications. Geraldo Perdomo, Lars Nootbar and Arenado had three hits each and McCann and Pavin Smith finished with two hits apiece for the D-backs. Cole Carrigg homered among his four hits, Kyle Karros and Zac Veen also homered and had two hits and Connor Norby and TJ Rumfield contributed two hits for Colorado (57-102), which had 17 hits. Arizona sent nine batters to the plate in the first inning against right-hander Tanner Gordon. Moreno's three-run homer started the scoring, Perdomo tripled, Smith singled and Arenado homered to cap the inning. It was Arenado's 29th home run of the season. Arizona scored twice in the second on an RBI double from Ketel Marte and a run-scoring single by Perdomo. Smith had an RBI double in the fourth and scored on McCann's single for a 10-0 advantage. Gordon (1-6) allowed 10 runs on 12 hits in 4 1/3 innings. D-backs starter Eduardo Rodriguez (16-7) allowed two runs on nine hits in six innings. The Rockies broke through against the left-hander when they loaded the bases with no outs in the fourth but managed just one run. McCann hit his sixth home run leading off the sixth inning and Karros homered in the bottom of the frame, his 13th. Hunter Goodman added an RBI single in the seventh and Carrigg hit a three-run shot later in the inning, his 11th of the year, for a 12-6 deficit. Veen hit a solo shot and Rumfield added an RBI double in the eighth. --Field Level Media

item.title: CONSOLIDA Cúpula Trump-Xi em Washington é marcada por grande alarde, mas tem pouca substância
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, recebeu o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, na Casa Branca nesta quinta-feira para uma luxuosa cúpula de Estado repleta de simbolismo, mas com pouca substância, sem sinais de que uma reunião a portas fechadas tenha gerado avanços em questões espinhosas como inteligência artificial, comércio, Taiwan e a guerra com o Irã.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt, David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, recebeu o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, na Casa Branca nesta quinta-feira para uma luxuosa cúpula de Estado repleta de simbolismo, mas com pouca substância, sem sinais de que uma reunião a portas fechadas tenha gerado avanços em questões espinhosas como inteligência artificial, comércio, Taiwan e a guerra com o Irã. Durante uma conversa bilateral à tarde, Xi instou os EUA a se oporem à “independência de Taiwan”, de acordo com um comunicado da agência oficial de notícias chinesa Xinhua logo após o término do encontro. A Casa Branca não divulgou imediatamente seu próprio resumo das conversações. Esperava-se que Xi pressionasse Trump nesta semana para suspender a venda de armas a Taiwan. Após sua visita à China em maio, Trump afirmou que estava suspendendo um pacote de armas para Taiwan no valor de cerca de US$14 bilhões e chamou isso de “um excelente trunfo nas negociações”. Essa medida deixou alguns aliados dos EUA na Ásia e até mesmo alguns pares republicanos de Trump preocupados com a possibilidade de ele se sentir tentado a amenizar o apoio de Washington a Taipé em troca de ganhos econômicos. A China reivindica Taiwan, governada democraticamente, como seu próprio território e não descartou o uso da força para obter o controle sobre a ilha. A cúpula entre os dois líderes ocorreu logo após Trump ter defendido veementemente o uso do poder militar em um discurso na ONU na terça-feira, sugerindo que poderia “aniquilar” o Irã. Ele adotou um tom notavelmente diferente com Xi nesta quinta-feira, refletindo um equilíbrio de poder que se deslocou em favor do líder chinês após uma guerra comercial que terminou com um recuo dos EUA em relação às tarifas. Em declarações após a chegada de Xi nesta quinta-feira, Trump enfatizou sua “amizade verdadeiramente grande” com Xi, em vez de se concentrar nas diferenças políticas, e disse que as duas potências haviam feito avanços no comércio desde sua viagem à China em maio. “Durante esta visita, também discutiremos questões urgentes relacionadas à segurança, tecnologia e ‘superinteligência’”, disse Trump, usando seu nome alternativo para inteligência artificial. Em declarações um pouco mais diretas, Xi afirmou que os interesses dos dois países estavam profundamente entrelaçados e que a competição entre eles deveria ser “saudável”. As empresas norte-americanas eram bem-vindas na China, disse ele, acrescentando que espera que “as empresas chinesas sejam tratadas de forma justa aqui nos Estados Unidos”. Xi também disse que os militares de ambos os países devem manter um diálogo regular para melhorar a prevenção de crises. Edgard Kagan, ex-autoridade da Casa Branca para o Leste Asiático, disse que a retórica contrastante demonstra a estratégia diferente de cada líder. “O presidente está apresentando a questão principalmente como uma questão de seu relacionamento pessoal com Xi”, disse Kagan, que agora trabalha no Centro de Estudos Estratégicos e Internacionais. “O que achei interessante foi que Xi está sendo muito mais cauteloso e sugerindo que se trata menos de um relacionamento pessoal e mais de um relacionamento entre as nações.” A cúpula, que marca a primeira visita de Xi a Washington em mais de uma década, é o segundo encontro deste ano entre os líderes das duas maiores economias do mundo. POMPA E CIRCUNSTÂNCIA Para Trump, que aprecia cerimônias e valoriza seus laços com líderes poderosos, a visita é tanto uma questão de prestígio nacional quanto uma oportunidade para uma diplomacia de alto nível. Mas as declarações de Trump e Xi não foram transmitidas ao vivo por nenhuma rede de televisão dos EUA, que se recusaram a fornecer imagens em protesto contra a proibição imposta pela Casa Branca à CNN, à MS Now e ao Politico. Trump recebeu Xi na chegada na noite de quarta-feira com um tapete vermelho na pista, a primeira vez que um presidente dos EUA recebe um líder estrangeiro na Base Conjunta Andrews desde que o presidente Barack Obama se encontrou com o papa Francisco em 2015, segundo a C-SPAN. Após suas declarações nesta quinta-feira, os dois líderes assistiram a uma cerimônia militar que incluiu uma exibição aérea no Jardim das Rosas. Após a reunião a portas fechadas, Trump levou Xi para conhecer o novo heliporto que havia construído recentemente no gramado sul da Casa Branca. “Ele adora granito de boa qualidade”, disse Trump aos repórteres, acrescentando que os dois tiveram uma “ótima reunião”, sem dar mais detalhes. A aproximação de Trump com Xi pode complicar sua mensagem de campanha nos Estados Unidos antes das eleições de meio de mandato de novembro, quando a estreita maioria republicana no Congresso estará em jogo, enquanto os eleitores se preocupam com a inflação e a guerra contra o Irã. Há meses, o presidente vem rotulando os democratas de “comunistas” em uma tentativa de retratá-los como extremistas, mas recebeu Xi, o líder do Partido Comunista Chinês, como um querido amigo pessoal, com bandeiras chinesas enfeitando o telhado acima do Salão Oval ao lado das bandeiras dos EUA. AVANÇOS POUCO PROVÁVEIS Apesar do alarde, grandes avanços pareciam improváveis, segundo analistas. O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, disse à Fox News na quarta-feira, após conversas com o vice-primeiro-ministro chinês He Lifeng, que eles haviam concordado em prorrogar até 10 de janeiro um acordo que suspende a guerra comercial entre os dois países. Trump escreveu em uma postagem no Truth Social na manhã desta quinta-feira que os dois líderes discutiriam a “superinteligência”, mas mais uma vez demonstrou pouco interesse em novas regulamentações, apesar das preocupações dos líderes do setor de que a IA possa, eventualmente, representar uma ameaça aos seres humanos. “A superinteligência (SI) será um grande tema de discussão, mas quero deixar isso exatamente como está”, escreveu Trump. “Essa também é a posição da China.” Durante seus comentários nesta quinta-feira, Xi disse que ambos os países devem “garantir que o desenvolvimento da IA esteja sempre sob controle humano”. Analistas afirmam que a intensa competição entre as duas potências no campo da IA provavelmente limitará o alcance de qualquer pacto além de acordos simbólicos. MANTER OS LAÇOS ESTÁVEIS Pessoas a par dos planos afirmam que as negociações também poderiam resultar em acordos para reduzir algumas tarifas, combater o tráfico de drogas e ampliar o diálogo entre os militares, enquanto se espera que Trump busque a libertação de norte-americanos e outras pessoas detidas na China. Xi parece estar em uma posição mais forte, tendo supervisionado um aumento no comércio da China e mantendo firme o controle sobre o fornecimento de minerais de terras raras, o que lhe dá uma poderosa vantagem. Ambos os líderes veem vantagens em manter as relações estáveis, com Trump atolado na impopular guerra contra o Irã e Xi enfrentando desafios econômicos internos. Mas, por trás das aparências, há desafios que poderiam reacender as tensões, incluindo disputas sobre Taiwan, controles de exportação, inteligência artificial e a guerra contra o Irã, um aliado da China. Há poucos sinais de que Pequim esteja disposta a exercer pressão sobre o Irã para que ceda às exigências dos EUA. Durante a reunião desta quinta-feira, Xi expressou apoio para que os EUA e o Irã retornem ao cessar-fogo e, eventualmente, negociem um acordo de paz, informou a Xinhua. A lista de convidados para o jantar de Estado desta quinta-feira inclui CEOs como Tim Cook, da Apple; Jeff Bezos, da Amazon; Sundar Pichai, da Alphabet; Sam Altman, da OpenAI; Elon Musk, da Tesla; e Jensen Huang, da Nvidia. Apesar desse leque de nomes, pessoas a par dos planos dos EUA afirmam que Trump provavelmente manterá controles rígidos sobre as exportações de tecnologia norte-americana — controles que Xi deseja que sejam flexibilizados.

item.title: Law firms vie for tech talent in AI race
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) As major companies and startups compete to hire engineers and data scientists to fuel the AI boom, David Wang is hoping to lure technologists to his law firm instead. Cooley, where Wang serves as chief innovation officer, is hiring for more than a dozen high-tech positions amid an escalating AI push at big law firms. The Palo Alto-based firm this month unveiled a new subsidiary it describes as a “firm-owned artificial intelligence company,” Cooley AI, to build internal tools for its lawyers and reshape how it delivers legal services. Wang said Cooley AI will be managed like a startup but integrated with the law firm's decision-making, a mix he said could appeal to AI and other experts who want a job that lets them apply their work directly to legal challenges. "You want people that want to work on really frontier difficult problems, and that is something that is hard for a law firm to promise," he said. The pitch to technical and legal talent is that Cooley AI is the "best of both worlds," Wang said, connecting hires with the law firm's business while offering meaningful work on cutting-edge AI issues. The launch of Cooley AI coincided with the firm's September 17 announcement of a product developed with OpenAI to help companies go public, for use by the firm’s attorneys in client work. It was timed with OpenAI's [USN:L6N45917D TEXT:"release"] of a legal industry-focused version of its latest AI technology, GPT-6 Astra, that it said is designed to help law firms and legal software providers conduct research, draft advice and build custom applications for lawyers. OpenAI said it has also been working with other big law firms on new tools, including Ropes & Gray and Sullivan & Cromwell. Law firms across the board are hiring technologists and strategists to staff AI and technology teams. Covington & Burling; Cravath, Swaine & Moore; Latham & Watkins; Kirkland & Ellis; McGuireWoods; Mayer Brown and White & Case are among those that are currently advertising AI-related job roles on LinkedIn. Salaries range per position, with one firm offering up to $438,000 for a director of applied AI. Cooley, known for its work advising technology and life sciences companies, is currently hiring for 14 roles within Cooley AI, including for senior engineers. At least four hires have already joined, including from other law firms, according to LinkedIn posts. Wang said Cooley AI just hired an engineer from Adobe and that other hires are in the works from large technology companies and startups. He declined to comment on compensation for new hires but said that "the market price is the market price. We're planning to be competitive." The firm's advertised salary ranges on LinkedIn included $220,000 to $250,000 for a senior AI data engineer. That pay would be roughly commensurate to a first-year lawyer's salary at Cooley and other large firms. The race among law firms to incorporate AI has led some firms to publicize their spending on the technology. Kirkland & Ellis in May said it plans to [USN:L6N4251D3 TEXT:"devote $500 million"] of its revenue to developing a custom AI platform over the next three to four years. Personal injury firm Morgan & Morgan has [USN:L6N4560UK TEXT:"committed at least $1 billion"] over the next decade, the firm said this month. Cooley declined to comment about the scale of its investment in Cooley AI. Some law firms, meanwhile, are losing lawyers to AI companies. Forty-six lawyers from the top 200 highest-grossing firms in the United States in the first half of 2026 moved to companies including Harvey, Anthropic and OpenAI, according to a report published on Thursday by legal analytics company Firm Prospects. SEYFARTH SUED AFTER DISCLOSING DATA SECURITY BREACH Law firm Seyfarth Shaw was sued on Thursday by a former employee of one of the law firm's clients who said a recently disclosed cybersecurity incident exposed sensitive personal information belonging to more than 56,000 people. The proposed class action was filed in federal court in Chicago shortly after the firm [USN:L6N45F0WX TEXT:"reported the breach"] to state regulators. The plaintiff is a former employee of AAA Mountain West Group, according to the lawsuit. The Chicago-founded firm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The firm in a statement this week said the data security incident was isolated to a single employee, and that the firm's security controls prevented access to the firm’s network or systems. 3M ORDERED TO PAY $296,000 TO ILLINOIS' LAWYERS AT DICELLO LEVITT A federal judge in Illinois has ordered 3M to pay nearly $296,000 in legal fees to plaintiffs firm DiCello Levitt, which is representing the state on a contingency basis in a lawsuit alleging contamination from "forever chemicals." US District Judge Sara Darrow in the federal court in Rock Island, Illinois, ruled that the contingency-fee lawyers could recover fees for work related to 3M's unsuccessful effort to move the case from state to federal court. The judge awarded DiCello Levitt $295,933 for about 285 hours of work on the removal dispute. Darrow said courts within the 7th US Circuit Court of Appeals have allowed such awards, even though the appeals court has not directly addressed the issue. Illinois sued 3M in 2022 over alleged contamination of drinking water, soil and air. 3M has denied wrongdoing and has appealed the ruling sending the case back to Illinois state court. The company opposed the state's recovery of fees. 3M and the Illinois attorney general’s office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. item.title: China's Jinzhao to begin construction of Peru port in 2027, minister says
item.description: Chinese firm Jinzhao will begin construction of a $405 million port in southern Peru in 2027, Peruvian Transportation Minister Jose Tangherlini said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese firm Jinzhao will begin construction of a $405 million port in southern Peru in 2027, Peruvian Transportation Minister Jose Tangherlini said on Thursday. The project, set to become Peru's third-largest port, will proceed after the government secured a land-transfer deal with Shougang Hierro Peru. Construction is expected to last approximately two years in its first stage, with an initial investment of $200 million, Tangherlini said. Under the agreement, signed with state investment promotion agency Proinversion, Shougang — which held a concession over part of the land — committed to not exercising its mining rights within the project area. The port is part of Jinzhao's broader development plan that includes the Pampa de Pongo iron ore project in southern Peru, with an investment of $1.78 billion. Jinzhao will become the second Chinese company to build and operate a port in Peru, one of the world's largest copper producers. Cosco Shipping Ports' Peruvian subsidiary has operated the Chancay "megaport" in northern Peru since late 2024, which is becoming a hub on the South American Pacific coast.

item.title: China Jinzhao comenzaría el próximo año la construcción de un nuevo puerto en Perú: ministro
item.description: La empresa china Jinzaho iniciará en el 2027 la construcción de un puerto de 405 millones de dólares en el sur del país para exportar minerales y otros productos, dijo el jueves el ministro de Transporte y Comunicaciones de Perú, José Tangherlini.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La empresa china Jinzaho iniciará en el 2027 la construcción de un puerto de 405 millones de dólares en el sur del país para exportar minerales y otros productos, dijo el jueves el ministro de Transporte y Comunicaciones de Perú, José Tangherlini. La ejecución del proyecto, que Jinzhao ganó en marzo en una licitación, será posible tras la firma de un convenio entre el Gobierno y la china Shougang Hierro Perú (SHPC1.LM) , que permitirá la entrega del terreno donde se construirá el terminal marítimo, que espera ser el tercer mayor del país, añadió el ministro. Según el convenio firmado con la agencia estatal promotora Proinversión, Shougang -que tenía en concesión de parte del terreno- se comprometió a no ejercer sus derechos mineros dentro del área del proyecto de puerto, agregó Tangherlini. "El próximo año ya estaría iniciando la construcción del mismo y hay un plazo estimado de que dure la construcción de aproximadamente dos años, en su primera etapa", dijo a periodistas el ministro tras la firma del acuerdo. En la primera etapa se invertirá 200 millones de dólares, agregó. El puerto de Jinzhao forma parte de un plan integral de la firma china que tiene el proyecto de hierro Pampa de Pongo, en el sur del país con una inversión de 1.781 millones de dólares. Jinzhao se convertirá en la segunda empresa china que construirá y operará un puerto en Perú, uno de los mayores productores de cobre en el mundo. Actualmente, la filial de la china Cosco Shipping Ports (1199.HK) opera desde fines del 2024 el "megapuerto" Chancay en el norte de Perú, que está convirtiéndose en un hub portuario en el Pacífico sudamericano.

item.title: Anthropic seeks 50.1% voting control for co-founders ahead of IPO, The Information reports
item.description: Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a new corporate structure that would award CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power, The Information reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the planning.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a new corporate structure that would award CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power, The Information reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the planning. The new arrangement, which emulates a founder-control structure at Palantir, would award the co-founders a special class of shares giving them collective voting control in most corporate matters, and would apply as long as three of the seven co-founders retain a minimum number of shares in the company, according to the report. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. One significant exception to the founders' control is the election of the members on Anthropic's board, which has seven seats, one of which is currently vacant, according to the report. The company is also planning to give employees a special class of stock that would serve as tie-breaker votes on some corporate issues, the report said. Anthropic, which has been viewed for months as the leader in enterprise AI, is preparing for what could be one of the biggest IPOs on record. The company could push its IPO to after the US midterm elections in November, with the poll not expected to have a major impact on the offering, Reuters [USN:L6N45818P TEXT:"reported"] earlier this month. The Claude maker had [USN:L4N4251V1 TEXT:"raised"] $65 billion at a post-money valuation of $965 billion in May.

item.title: Lula mantém vantagem de 2 pontos sobre Flávio no 2º turno com 47% a 45%, mostra Datafolha
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) manteve vantagem numérica de dois pontos sobre o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial, e os dois candidatos seguem em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) manteve vantagem numérica de dois pontos sobre o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial, e os dois candidatos seguem em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira. Lula tem 47% e Flávio soma 45%. Na semana passada, o placar era de 46% a 44% a favor do petista. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, para cima ou para baixo. Aqueles que declaram voto em branco, nulo ou em nenhum dos dois candidatos diminuíram um ponto, para 7%. Os indecisos seguem registrando 1%. No cenário de primeiro turno, o presidente soma 40%, ante 39% na sondagem anterior, enquanto o senador do PL tem 36%, repetindo o número da semana passada. A distância entre os dois neste cenário, de 4 pontos percentuais, está no limite da margem de erro. Na terceira colocação vem Augusto Cury (Avante), com 5% -- eram 6%, na rodada passada --, seguido de Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), com os mesmos 4% aferidos na última semana. Os demais candidatos não pontuaram acima dos 3%. Aqueles que declaram votos em branco, nulos ou em nenhum dos nomes colocados somam 5%, ante 6% na pesquisa anterior. Os indecisos ficaram em 2%, ante 3% na semana passada. O Datafolha também levantou as intenções de voto em uma resposta espontânea, sem oferecer uma lista com os nomes dos candidatos. Neste cenário, Lula tem 36% (eram 35%), Flávio registra 27% (ante 26%), e o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, pai de Flávio, é citado por 4%. Os demais não superaram o patamar dos 3%. O percentual de indecisos, que era de 21% na semana passada, agora soma 18%, enquanto a fatia do eleitorado que pretende votar em branco, nulo ou em nenhum dos colocados passou de 6% para 5%. A sondagem apontou que 80% dos eleitores estão totalmente decididos sobre o candidato em que vão votar para presidente. Os outros 20% ainda podem mudar seu voto. O instituto também apurou a rejeição aos candidatos, situação em que Lula e Flávio aparecem novamente empatados, com 45% cada. Na rodada anterior, os dois também encontravam-se empatados: 47% dos entrevistados declararam que não votariam de jeito nenhum em Lula ou em Flávio. APROVAÇÃO DO GOVERNO Ainda de acordo com a pesquisa, a aprovação do governo sofreu uma leve variação. Os mesmos 50% que desaprovavam o governo na semana passada foram registrados agora, enquanto a parcela dos que aprovam a gestão oscilou de 48% para 47%. Os que não souberam responder mantiveram-se no patamar de 3%. No quesito avaliação de governo, 40% o consideram "ruim" ou "péssimo" ante 42% na semana passada; 34% o avaliam como "ótimo" ou "bom", mesma fatia verificada na rodada anterior; 24% classificam o governo como "regular" -- eram 23% --, e 2% não souberam responder, percentual que há uma semana marcava 1%. O Datafolha ouviu 2.002 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 22 e 23 de setembro.

item.content:encoded: La provincia argentina de San Juan, rica en proyectos mineros, informó el jueves que colocó un bono internacional por 600 millones de dólares con una tasa del cupón del 9,55%.
